newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says will review 2-tier baht/dlr market.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says will review 2-tier baht/dlr market.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Tuesday it would review its two-tier baht/dollar exchange rate system from time to time by taking into account market sentiment and Thailand's economic performance.

Assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee told reporters: "We will review the measure from time to time, by looking at market sentiment and (the government) handling of economic problems on whether it boosts investor confidence."
The assistant governor did not indicate how often the bank would review the measure or when it may be lifted.
Thailand earlier this month asked local banks to help block access of short-term baht funds used by foreign speculators after they launched speculative attacks on the Thai currency.

Thai-based commercial banks have been asked to quote exorbitant baht/dollar swap rates for foreign clients since May 15 which effectively raised to over 1,000 percent the annualised funding cost for hedge funds to speculate against the baht.
Dealers said the measure dried up short-term baht funds used by speculators to attack the currency.
On Tuesday, Siri described the central bank measure as over 90 percent effective.
The official said with normal market sentiment in the future, Thailand would again look at foreign exchange control systems in other countries. He did not elaborate.

Central bank sources have voiced concern that the two-tier exchange rate system, if adopted over extended periods, may leave Thailand with a balance of payments deficit problem as it would hamper foreign capital inflows.
